newsitem.title: INDONESIA: INDONESIA LATE PALM OLEIN STABLE, TALK OF BULOG.
newsitem.headline: INDONESIA LATE PALM OLEIN STABLE, TALK OF BULOG.

text.p: Indonesian palm olein prices were generally stable in late trading, with demand weakening amid falls in Malaysia, traders said.

They said palm olein was quoted at 1,495-1,500 rupiah/kg in Jakarta, unchanged from the opening, but trades were also heard at 1,490 rupiah. Crude palm oil was done at 1,246 rupiah/kg at a 500-tonne tender in the north Sumatran city of Medan. A second tender for a similar amount was cancelled when the top bid of 1,231 rupiah fell short of the seller's expectations of 1,246.
"Demand was not very good today because of the weak market in Malaysia," one trader said. "Supply in Jakarta also seems to be improving, with a few shipments coming in."
The traders said there was market talk that state logistics agency BULOG had purchased 8,500 tonnes of palm olein in Malaysia and that the oil was expected here later this month.
"There has been talk of BULOG buying oil in Malaysia and this has raised concern in the market over whether BULOG is going to intervene," one trader said.
BULOG had previously indicated that it preferred to see palm olein prices keep below the 1,500-rupiah level.

Data from Belawan Port showed that the MT Amer Rhina left for Kandla port in India last Sunday with 6,000 tonnes of palm oil, while the MT Lissom left for Rotterdam on Monday with 12,500 tonnes of palm kernel expeller.
The MT Freja Jutiandio will leave on Tuesday for Algeria with 2,100 tonnes of palm oil, while the MT Friends Forever left for India on Monday with 4,500 tonnes of palm oil.
The MT Maharani will leave for Tanjung Priok on Wednesday with 1,000 tonnes of palm olein.
